1.point: Open with a hook and announce that the chapter will show the difference between knowing about God and knowing Him, recalling earlier ground briefly.
steps: A concrete image of knowing from the inside (hunger in Ramadan)
Most religious knowledge is knowledge about God; the Qur'an's invitation (earlier ground) is to know Him as hunger is known
State what the chapter will establish

2.point: The gnostic knows God by being present to Him, not by fitting Him into a definition.
steps: Define acquired knowledge: from outside, via concepts
Acquired knowledge works by definition, and definition is limitation
Define knowledge by presence: within the soul, no concept, examples
Mysticism aims at arriving by presence, not understanding by definition; God has no limit, so definition cannot reach Him
Therefore the arif knows God by presence

3.point: Reason knows only attributes and never essence, still less God's, so if God is to be known it must be within the soul.
steps: Reason knows attributes, not what a thing is (Ibn Sina)
A fortiori it cannot reach God (Imam Ali's oration)
Reason's remaining work on God is proof of existence and negations: knowledge about
Irfan wants positive knowledge of God's attributes, which only presence gives
Presence is only of what is within us; a sense of God is within us; so God is known within the soul

4.point: Knowledge of God is a light that God places in a heart that has been purified; it is not gathered by study.
steps: Knowledge analysis cannot produce must be given; a hadith names the giver
The hadith contrasts gathered learning with light placed by God
'Whomever He wills' seems to make it arbitrary; the Nur verse is brought in
Resolution: God withholds nothing; what keeps a heart dark is that it is closed; the traveller opens it
Opening is purifying; purification is followed by divine teaching (Khomeini, Baqarah verse)

5.point: The way to know God is purification (wayfaring), which begins with the shari'a; study tells the traveller what to practise but cannot stand in for purification.
steps: If the light is everywhere and the heart closed, the path is opening the heart: suluk not fikr
Wayfaring is purify and then wait; the Munajat ties light to the path
The path begins with the shari'a: doing what the Prophet asked
Practice needs knowledge of the rules, so study has an early place (Tabataba'i)
Study without faith is a veil, yet one approaches the veil to tear it: study serves and cannot replace

6.point: Summarise: knowing God is a different kind of knowing, reached by purification, served but not replaced by study.
steps: Restate the chapter's conclusion
Bridge to the next chapter

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Supplies the hook and the hunger image the whole chapter leans on; introduces the idea of knowing from the inside.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Names the two kinds of knowing, recalls the Qur'an's invitation from earlier ground in one sentence, and states what the chapter will establish.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Defines acquired knowledge: from outside, through concepts. First step of the contrast.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Adds that acquired knowledge works by definition and that definition is limitation (hadd). This link is what later rules out defining God.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Defines knowledge by presence and gives the examples (self, hunger, pain, anxiety) the argument reuses.

¶6.label: aside
¶6.why: The completeness and incorrigibility of knowledge by presence (one cannot be wrong that one feels hungry) is true and well put, but no later sentence in this or any later section uses it; delete it and ¶7 still follows from ¶5. Borderline support at most.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Supplies the decisive step: mysticism aims at arriving by presence, not understanding by definition, and God has no limit, so definition cannot reach Him. The section's point lands here.

¶8.label: restate
¶8.why: Imam Khomeini drawing 'the same line' says again what ¶7 has just concluded; the gnostic-versus-scholar pairing adds the word 'arif but no new link. A second authority confirming a point already made.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Reason knows attributes, never what the thing is; Ibn Sina grants it. First step of the section.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Moves from things to God a fortiori and introduces the oration that will carry the step.

¶11.label: support
¶11.why: Reads the displayed quotation and ties it back to definition-as-limit from ¶4; the quotation would hang unused without it.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: New step: what reason can still do about God is prove existence and negate; all of it is knowledge about, and negative.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Supplies the turn: irfan wants the positive side, the attributes known from within, which is knowledge by presence. The Mulla Sadra sentence and the 'bewildered' quotation are extra weight inside an otherwise needed paragraph.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Closes the chain: presence is only of what is within us, a sense of God is within us, so God is known within the soul.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: What analysis cannot produce must be given; introduces the hadith that names the giver.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Reads the hadith: learning is gathered, the light is placed by God in the heart. Supplies the 'light' half of the point.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Raises the objection the point must clear (does God choose arbitrarily?) and brings in the verse used to answer it.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Answers the objection: God withholds nothing; a dark heart is a closed heart; the traveller's work is to open it. This is the step that makes 'purified heart' a condition rather than a lottery.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Opening is purifying, and purification is followed by divine teaching (Khomeini). Introduces the Baqarah verse. Completes the point.

¶20.label: restate
¶20.why: Glosses the verse but says only what ¶19 has already said (teaching follows wariness, light to the pure). The verse could stand on ¶19's introduction alone.

¶21.label: aside
¶21.why: How the knowledge travels (heart to heart, through a guide) is a new topic the point does not need; it belongs to Chapter Seven, which it already defers to. Nothing later depends on it.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Draws the consequence of Section 4: the path is opening the heart; names suluk against fikr. First step.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Wayfaring has two parts, purify and wait; introduces the Munajat line that ties light to path.

¶24.label: support
¶24.why: Reads the displayed prayer line and names who receives the light (the one on God's path), which is what the quotation is there to show for ¶22-23.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: New step: the path begins with the shari'a, doing what the Prophet asked; without it no ma'rifah.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: Supplies study's role: practice needs knowledge of the rules, so study comes early and feeds action (Tabataba'i). The 'study serves' half of the point.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: Supplies the 'cannot replace' half: learning without faith is a veil, yet one approaches it to tear it. The final sentence then states the conclusion, which is the only place it is stated in full.

¶28.label: restate
¶28.why: A closing summary that repeats the conclusions of Sections 2, 3, 4 and 5 (presence, hunger, light, purified heart). Nothing new.

¶29.label: aside
¶29.why: Raises a question the chapter does not answer; a bridge to the next chapter, not a link in this one.
